messages: Subject: Commercial terms: staged commit, invoicing path & tax residency

Sara — attaching a draft redline of the Order Form so we can lock down commercials and hand off to legal/finance. Key changes in this draft: 
- Staged commit: 3-month pilot (no commit), then a 9-month ramped minimum commitment (see pricing schedule tab).
- Pricing schedule: monthly SKU breakdown with per-token rates that step down at three thresholds.
- Invoicing: standard monthly invoices in arrears; draft assumes Net 45.
- Taxes: draft says customer is responsible for applicable VAT/GST; Redwood will collect taxes unless customer provides valid VAT/Tax registration evidence prior to first invoice.

Asks from our side:
1) Can procurement confirm whether Everwell requires invoices to be issued to a particular legal entity and whether you will provide a PO for the committed tranche?
2) Please confirm tax residency for your billing entity (W-9 or W-8 / EU VAT ID). If you can share the W-9/VAT ID we will mark invoices accordingly.
3) Any internal constraints on Net terms (Net 30/45/60)?

I cc Monica/Kimberly to loop Finance and Legal on the redline. Next steps: if commercial language looks OK we’ll circulate to Legal for a clean MSA redline and then share a final Order Form for signature.

Attachments: draft_order_form_redline.docx

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the redline. A few quick notes from procurement side: 
- We will need Net 60 on our side (standard for our vendor cohort).
- We must issue a PO prior to any committed tranche billing. I’m attaching our PO template for your invoice team.
- We need a per-month SKU breakdown (line items) and a sample invoice that shows the PO number, tax lines (VAT), and payment remittance instructions.
- On tax: Everwell is an EU legal entity for these services; we will supply a VAT ID (and confirm if an intra-EU reverse charge applies). If Redwood needs to issue invoices from an EU subsidiary, flag that — procurement will escalate.

I’ll loop finance directly (procurement@everwellhealth.com) if we proceed. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept Net 60 for the first 6 months or if you need a shorter Net term.

Team — quick internal read: good progress. A few legal/finance suggestions before we reply to Sara: 
1) Net terms: Finance prefers Net 45 standard. If procurement needs Net 60, we can accept for the first two invoices but not as a permanent concession without revenue protection (e.g., invoice-level interest on late payments or a partial upfront credit).
2) Tax/VAT: add mandatory clause that customer must provide valid tax registration evidence (VAT ID/W-9) before first invoice; otherwise Redwood will charge VAT and remit it.
3) Entity/invoicing: we should capture the exact legal entity name/registration to avoid tax reissuance later. If Everwell requires EU invoicing, escalate to Legal — we have an EU entity but need to confirm pricing tables map to that entity (pricing currency differences).
4) PO: require the PO number on the invoice and include a short acceptance window (14 days) after which fees are considered undisputed unless disputed in writing.

I put inline comments in the Google Doc redline: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-orderform-redline (Legal: please review MSA changes re: invoice-splitting across entities).

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance & Operations | Redwood Inference
Subject: Re: Commercial terms: staged commit, invoicing path & tax residency

Sara — appreciate the quick turnaround. Proposed pragmatic path to unblock procurement/finance: 
- Redwood accepts Net 60 for the first two invoices while Everwell completes PO and tax evidence collection; thereafter invoices will move to Net 45.
- Everwell to provide PO number before the first committed-tranche invoice is issued; we will include PO on all invoices.
- Tax evidence (VAT ID or W-9): required before the first billed month for committed spend. If not provided, Redwood will apply VAT and remit as required.

I’ve attached a tightened Order Form redline that implements the above and includes a sample invoice layout. If that aligns, we’ll have Legal produce a final MSA redline and Finance will prepare the sample invoice template to share with procurement.
